sections.overview: Udea lutealis is a crambid moth recorded widely in Europe and common in Britain.
sections.identification: The adult has pale cream forewings with darker cross-lines and outlined markings.
sections.habitat: It occurs in varied open and semi-open settings, including meadows, field edges and woodland margins.
sections.diet: The caterpillars feed on many herbaceous plants, including bramble, plantain, thistles and sorrel.
sections.behavior: Adults fly at night, chiefly in midsummer.
sections.reproduction: The caterpillars are reported in spring; the consulted accounts do not give a reliable egg count or detailed mating description.
sections.ecology: Larvae may shelter in a light web beneath a leaf, and may roll narrow leaves into a tube.
sections.conservation: It is described as very common in Britain, but that regional description is not a global conservation assessment.
